titleEn: I Thought You Were Bringing It

pages.text: There was one ball in the village. Until yesterday, it had been on Mumu's porch. Someone had to bring it for a ball game.
"Let's play ball tomorrow!" Taro said. "Okay!" Mumu raised a hand.
Taro thought Mumu would bring it, because it was at Mumu's house. Mumu thought Taro would bring it, because he had suggested the game.
Taro came to the tree empty-handed. "We'll start as soon as Mumu comes."
Mumu came to the tree empty-handed. "We'll start as soon as Taro comes."
Taro looked at Mumu's empty hands. "You brought it, right?"
Mumu looked at Taro's empty hands. "You brought it, right?"
"I thought you were bringing it!" they both said. They showed each other their open palms.
The sun was already sinking. Mumu glanced toward home. If they went back now, there would be no time left to play.
Taro rolled a coconut. But it did not roll smoothly. It stopped with a bump. They both held their bellies and laughed.
